content:
The image shows a mango leaf with dark, irregular black patches scattered across the surface. The spots are dark/black, appear superficial (sooty/encrusted), and are distributed across the upper leaf surface without the characteristic sunken lesions, halos, or raised margins associated with other diseases.

Key observations:
- Black, soot-like dark patches on the leaf surface
- The underlying leaf tissue appears mostly intact and green
- No sunken lesions, no red halos, no angular raised margins
- The dark material appears to sit on top of the leaf surface rather than being embedded in tissue

This matches Sooty Mould: black encrustation on leaf surface formed by superficial dark mycelium growing on insect secretions, without direct tissue penetration.
